requirement.evidence: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
requirement.note: Core prohibition, written notice and opportunity to respond, and complaint filing are supported. But the card says 'to evict', while the document says 'terminate a tenancy', which is close. The 'where an exemption allows it' framing for the notice requirement is not stated; the document says notice applies to any action based on criminal history.

key_value.evidence: Any landlord found to be in violation of the Ordinance shall be subject to administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation
key_value.note: Fine range and the inquiry prohibition are both stated.

effective_date.note: Field is empty on the card.

status.evidence: On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106).
status.note: The document presents the ordinance as current law with no effective date given, so in_force is acceptable.

coverage.evidence: Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
coverage.note: The 3-unit owner-occupied exemption threshold is stated. No construction or certificate-of-occupancy cutoffs appear in the document.

citation.note: The document cites BMC 13.106, which matches the card's citation.
